BiblicalUsage: Chaphets is being pleased with, delighting in, desiring, and it describes God's pleasure and man's. The Lord whom ye seek shall suddenly come to His temple, even the messenger of the covenant whom ye delight in. Nehemiah prays for the servants who desire to fear God's name, the psalm says God has no pleasure in wickedness, and asks what man is he that desireth life and loveth many days.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe delight is the test of the heart: what I delight in is what I worship, whether it is the messenger of the covenant or a long life. God has no pleasure in wickedness, and neither should I. I hold that praying like Nehemiah, to be counted among those who desire to fear His name, is the right desire.
